source: ESPN public injury report and game summaries

injuries.name: P.J. Washington
injuries.short_comment: Washington (shoulder) is listed as questionable for Saturday's game versus the Clippers.
injuries.long_comment: Washington has had a productive 2026-27 campaign thus far, averaging 14.0 points, 6.7 rebounds, 1.3 assists and 1.1 blocks over 30.8 minutes per outing. He has also appeared in all 15 of the Mavericks' regular-season games, though he is in danger of missing Saturday's meeting with the Clippers. If Washington gets ruled out, more minutes should open up for Zaccharie Risacher and Naji Marshall.

injuries.name: Dereck Lively II
injuries.short_comment: Head coach Dusty May said Friday that Lively (foot) is moving well and progressing in his recovery, and the big man told May he's "close" to returning, Mike Curtis of The Dallas Morning News reports.
injuries.long_comment: Lively hasn't seen game action since Nov. 21, 2025, and he remains without a firm timetable to return after undergoing right foot surgery last December. However, this update suggests that the big man is trending in the right direction.

injuries.name: Walter Clayton Jr.
injuries.short_comment: Clayton (knee) is questionable for Saturday's game against the Clippers.
injuries.long_comment: Clayton is dealing with left knee tendinitis. Naji Marshall and Zaccharie Risacher would see more playing time off the bench if Clayton is downgraded to out Saturday.

injuries.name: Tobi Lawal
injuries.short_comment: Lawal (groin) is out for Saturday's game against the Clippers.
injuries.long_comment: Lawal will miss a second straight game with right groin tightness. The rookie forward isn't expected to have a big role in the rotation, so he likely won't have much fantasy upside anytime soon. His next chance to play will come Sunday against the Jazz on the second leg of a back-to-back set.

injuries.name: Tarik Biberovic
injuries.short_comment: Biberovic (heel) is out for Wednesday's game against the Warriors.
injuries.long_comment: Biberovic has yet to debut for the Mavs this season due to a right heel bursitis issue, and the fact that he continues to get ruled out a full day in advance of tipoff suggests he's still not close. Biberovic should be considered week-to-week moving forward.

injuries.name: Sergio de Larrea
injuries.short_comment: De Larrea (knee) is listed as out for Wednesday's game against the Warriors.
injuries.long_comment: De Larrea has only played four games during the 2026-27 campaign. There hasn't been any indication of when he will be cleared to return, so he should be considered week-to-week for now.

injuries.name: Brandon Ingram
injuries.short_comment: Ingram (Achilles) is expected to make his season and team debut Monday against the Rockets, per Shams Charania of ESPN.
injuries.long_comment: The star forward is set to make his long-awaited return after undergoing surgery for a partially torn Achilles tendon in May. Ingram, who'll miss Saturday's game in Dallas, is likely to carry a minutes restriction following a lengthy layoff, though his presence is certain to cut into the playing time of the likes of Kris Dunn, Max Strus and Gradey Dick on the wing for the Clippers.

injuries.name: Jordan Miller
injuries.short_comment: Miller underwent surgery Wednesday to repair a torn left rotator cuff and will be re-evaluated in six months, per Law Murray of The Athletic.
injuries.long_comment: It's a tough break for Miller, who had an opportunity to battle for a reserve role during training camp in the fall. The timeline for a return is likely to keep him on the shelf until after the All-Star break. Miller's extended stay on the sidelines gives Kobe Sanders a chance to crack the Clippers' rotation.

injuries.name: Bradley Beal
injuries.short_comment: Beal (knee) will not be ready for the start of the regular season, NBA writer Justin Russo reports.
injuries.long_comment: Beal is dealing with knee inflammation that will keep him sidelined for Opening Night. While it's unclear how long the Clippers will be without the veteran guard, Darius Garland, Keaton Wagler and Kris Dunn should dominate the backcourt minutes in his absence. Beal's 2025-26 campaign was cut short by a hip injury after he averaged 8.2 points and 1.7 assists in 20.6 minutes across just six regular-season appearances.
